title: Data Import, Export and Backup Workflows
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and value of Data Import, Export and Backup Workflows.
Apply data import, export and backup workflows to a Python project scenario.
Identify decisions and trade-offs relevant to data import, export and backup workflows.
Review common mistakes and risks in data import, export and backup workflows.
Produce a verifiable project artifact using data import, export and backup workflows principles.

understand.concept: Import and export workflows move data between application formats and external files. They need explicit schemas, encoding, validation, error reporting and safe handling of partial failure. Backups preserve recoverable copies and should be verified through restore tests.
understand.whyItMatters: Data exchange is only reliable when format assumptions, validation and recovery are designed explicitly.
understand.analogy: Moving items between containers requires labels, counts and checks at both ends.
understand.analogyLimit: A file copy is not automatically a consistent or restorable backup, especially while data is changing.
understand.summary: Data Import, Export and Backup Workflows helps learners deliver and maintain reliable Python projects.

explain.narrative: Define the import format and version, validate each record and report rejected rows without silently corrupting accepted data. Export stable fields and document encoding. For databases, use supported backup mechanisms or a consistent snapshot. Test restoration and protect backup access.
